finding.headline: At 62, the higher 401(k) catch-up limit of $11,750 for ages 60 to 63 applies to you in 2027.
details: The IRS passage says the higher catch-up limit for employees aged 60, 61, 62 and 63 is $11,750 for 2027, instead of $8,500.
You plan to retire at 64, so Medicare at 65 falls about one year after you stop work. Medicare says to sign up during your 7-month Initial Enrollment Period, which starts 3 months before you turn 65.
Social Security benefits rise for each month you delay past full retirement age, and the increase stops at age 70.

finding.headline: You can count on $233,700 a year: $66,900 for basics and $166,800 for the rest.
details: Your basics cost about $66,900 a year.
Your goal is $220,000 a year, which is below the $233,700 you can count on, so the goal works in 96 of 100 scenarios.

assumptions: All figures are in today's dollars: what money buys now, not the larger sums prices will reach.

Savings grow on average 5.0% a year above inflation in stocks and 1.8% in bonds, with good and bad years. The plan tests many possible market paths. These are planning figures, not a forecast. They are fixed, so every plan is tested on the same markets; to see a bad stretch, try a What If such as markets fall 30%.

Until you retire you save about $145,585 a year: $25,500 into a 401(k) or IRA, $11,400 from your employer's match, $108,685 of take-home pay left after your spending, which the plan assumes you save. If that is wrong, change 'Yearly saving' in your answers.
Pay stays at today's level until you retire, with no raises. This is fixed: raises are not certain, so the plan does not count on them. If your pay changes, change it in your answers.
Social Security uses the figure you gave, read as the benefit at 67. Your answers show $48,000 a year from 67. This plan starts it at 70, which pays about $59,500 a year.
If you retire before Medicare starts at 65, health cover costs about $10,000 a person a year until then (an assumption). Other health costs follow CMS figures by age.

Tax uses the 2027 federal brackets, the standard deduction and your state's rates. While you work, 401(k) saving comes off taxable pay. In retirement the plan counts 85% of Social Security as taxable, the most the law allows, so the tax may be a little high.
The plan runs to age 92. There is about a 1 in 4 chance that you will live that long (US life table, SOA 2024). People with more money tend to live longer than that table says.

actions.title: Use the higher 401(k) catch-up limit at ages 62 and 63.
actions.why: The 401(k) limit is $37,250 a year for ages 60 to 63, up from $34,000 at 50 and over. The plan is based on an example of a similar household, not your own, which kept the basics safest and left the most to spend.

actions.title: Plan health cover for the year before Medicare at 65.
actions.why: You retire at 64, so you have about one year without Medicare. Expect about $10,000 a year for health premiums, and sign up during your 7-month Initial Enrollment Period, which starts 3 months before you turn 65.

actions.title: Review the tax order for withdrawals each year.
actions.why: Draw on taxable savings and cash first, then your 401(k), then Roth accounts. Taxable savings are about 76% of your savings. Check the details with a tax professional before you act.

worth_checking.title: An income annuity
worth_checking.why: You are one person with savings that may not last in a long life. An income annuity trades part of your savings for a fixed sum each year for life. The sum loses value to inflation and the money cannot be taken back. This is information only. This is something to look into, not a recommendation. I have not priced it.
